why: ONE LIST, TWO READERS — the twin of fixtures/plates.json, for the same reason.
`accepted` IS WHETHER A VISIT CAN BE RECORDED AT ALL. The service answers yes to anything with
three characters (operations/api/v1/field.py), and the till answers yes to a visit with no phone
at all (till.py). The field screen used to answer yes only to a Saudi mobile, so a Gulf visitor,
a company landline, or a number typed with its country code left the save button dark with no
message — while the same customer could be recorded through the till without one.
`saudiMobile` IS A DIFFERENT QUESTION: can a reminder REACH this number. It is worth saying out
loud, because that is what the shop is paying for — but it is a warning on the screen, not a
refusal, and it is not the service's business at all.
arabic-indic-digits: intentional — quoted exactly as a keyboard produces them.

cases.note: same number, Arabic keyboard — folded before either question is asked
his own number with the country code: refused by the screen, accepted everywhere else
a company landline — a real customer who will not get reminders
a Gulf visitor, which is an ordinary thing in a workshop
too short for a mobile: recorded, and reported as unreachable rather than lost silently
below what the service itself accepts
